title: Lesson 7: Analysis of Karma — We Are the Owners of Our Deeds

suttaRef.title: The Shorter Exposition of Action (MN 135)
suttaRef.excerptPali: Kammassakā, māṇava, sattā kammadāyādā kammayoni kammabandhū kammapaṭisaraṇā. Kammaṃ satte vibhajati yadidaṃ hīnappaṇītatāyāti... Idhānanda, ekacco mātughātako hoti pitughātako... Idhānanda, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti...
suttaRef.excerptTranslation: Beings are owners of their actions, student, heirs of their actions; they originate from their actions, are bound to their actions, have their actions as their refuge. It is action that distinguishes beings as inferior and superior... Killing leads to short life, refraining from killing leads to long life; envy leads to powerlessness, lack of envy leads to high influence...

pariyatti.shortSummary: One of the most foundational discourses: The Buddha's reply to young Subha explaining human inequality (wealth, health, beauty, longevity, power). Devoid of divine favoritism or blind chance, disparities accurately reflect the gravitational momentum of intentional action (*Kamma*).

coreConcepts.definition: Every sentient agent bears 100% radical responsibility for bodily, verbal, and mental volitions.
Karmic fruit received today and tomorrow is inheritance generated by past choices.
Disparities in fortune, health, intelligence, and environment spring from variegated karmic sowing.

pariyatti.expositionMarkdown:
### 1. The Seven Karmic Pairs in MN 135
- Violence ➔ Short life | Non-violence ➔ Longevity
- Afflicting creatures ➔ Illness | Compassionate healing ➔ Robust health
- Chronic rage ➔ Unpleasant appearance | Loving serenity ➔ Radiant beauty
- Envy of others ➔ Powerlessness | Rejoicing in others' gain ➔ High influence
- Miserly greed ➔ Poverty | Generous giving ➔ Abundant prosperity
- Arrogant conceit ➔ Low birth | Humble reverence ➔ Noble respect
- Spiritual lethargy ➔ Stupidity | Inquiring inquiry ➔ Brilliant wisdom

### 2. The Sovereign Agency of Karma
The Buddha hands destiny entirely into your hands. Want health, prosperity, and respect? Beg no gods—sow the precise karmic seeds in your living present!

commonMisconceptions.mistake: Viewing karma as cosmic retribution or divine punishment.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Karma is neutral psychological physics. Sow chili seeds, harvest hot pepper; sow sugarcane, harvest sweetness.

commonMisconceptions.mistake: Self-righteously taunting someone in tragedy: 'Karma punished them!'.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Cruel gloating generates horrific unwholesome karma. Authentic practitioners radiate boundless compassion (*Karuṇā*), mindful of their own unripened debts.

patipatti.practiceGuide:
1. Daily Recitation of the 5 Reflections: Aging, Illness, Death, Separation, and Karmic Ownership.
2. Perform at least one selfless act of generosity or service today.
patipatti.suggestedVirtue: Impeccable ethical integrity and proactive cultivation of merit.

pativedha.reflectionPrompt: Do you realize your future destiny is not a murky gamble, but is being sketched with mathematical precision by your choices today?
selfAuditChecklist: I recited the Five Universal Reflections early morning.
I refrained from an unwholesome deed out of wise moral dread (*Ottappa*).
I rejoiced unreservedly in the success and good fortune of others.
